q.t: How many national parks are there, and in which parts of the UK?
q.e: There are 15 national parks in England, Wales and Scotland. They are areas of protected countryside that everyone can visit, and where people live, work and look after the landscape.
o: 15, in England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland

q.t: When was the National Trust founded, and by how many volunteers?
q.e: The National Trust was founded in 1895 by three volunteers. There are now more than 61,000 volunteers helping to keep the organisation running.

q.t: What is Big Ben?
q.e: Big Ben is the nickname for the great bell of the clock at the Houses of Parliament in London. Many people call the clock Big Ben as well. The clock is over 150 years old and is a popular tourist attraction.
o: The nickname for the great bell of the clock at the Houses of Parliament
The name of the clock tower at the Houses of Parliament
The largest Ferris wheel in London
The bell of St Paul's Cathedral

q.t: Why was the clock tower at the Houses of Parliament named 'Elizabeth Tower'?
q.e: The clock tower is named 'Elizabeth Tower' in honour of Queen Elizabeth II's Diamond Jubilee in 2012.
o: In honour of the Diamond Jubilee in 2012
Because Elizabeth I ordered it to be built
Because it was completed in the reign of Elizabeth I

q.t: Where is the Eden Project, and what are its biomes like?
q.e: The Eden Project is located in Cornwall, in the south west of England. Its biomes, which are like giant greenhouses, house plants from all over the world. The Eden Project is also a charity which runs environmental and social projects internationally.
o: In Cornwall, and its biomes are like giant greenhouses
In Wales, and its biomes are like giant greenhouses
In Cornwall, and its biomes are underground caves
In Cheshire, and its biomes are like giant greenhouses

q.t: The Giant's Causeway is on the coast of which part of the UK, and how was it formed?
q.e: Located on the north-east coast of Northern Ireland, the Giant's Causeway is a land formation of columns made from volcanic lava. It was formed about 50 million years ago.

q.t: Which of these statements is correct?
q.e: Loch Lomond is the largest expanse of fresh water in mainland Britain and probably the best-known part of the Loch Lomond and the Trossachs National Park. The Lake District is England's largest national park, and its biggest stretch of water is Windermere.
o: Loch Lomond is the largest expanse of fresh water in mainland Britain
Windermere is the largest expanse of fresh water in mainland Britain

q.t: On which river is the London Eye, and what was it originally built for?
q.e: The London Eye is situated on the southern bank of the River Thames and is a Ferris wheel. It was originally built as part of the UK's celebration of the new millennium and continues to be an important part of New Year celebrations.
o: The Thames, and it was built for the millennium
The Thames, and it was built for the 2012 Olympic Games
The Severn, and it was built for the millennium
The Thames, and it was built for the Diamond Jubilee

q.t: Snowdonia is a national park in which part of the UK, and what is its best-known landmark?
q.e: Snowdonia is a national park in North Wales. It covers an area of 838 square miles (2,170 square kilometres). Its most well-known landmark is Snowdon, which is the highest mountain in Wales.
o: North Wales, and its best-known landmark is Snowdon
Scotland, and its best-known landmark is Snowdon
North Wales, and its best-known landmark is Windermere
The Lake District, and its best-known landmark is Snowdon

q.t: Which TWO things can visitors see or do at the Tower of London?
q.e: The Tower of London was first built by William the Conqueror after he became king in 1066. Tours are given by the Yeoman Warders, also known as Beefeaters, who tell visitors about the building's history. People can also see the Crown Jewels there.
o: Take a tour given by the Yeoman Warders

q.t: Which lake was voted Britain's favourite view by television viewers in 2007?
q.e: The Lake District is England's largest national park. It is famous for its lakes and mountains. The biggest stretch of water is Windermere. In 2007, television viewers voted Wastwater as Britain's favourite view.

q.t: Which TWO famous gardens named in the handbook are in England?
q.e: There are famous gardens to visit throughout the UK, including Kew Gardens, Sissinghurst and Hidcote in England, Crathes Castle and Inveraray Castle in Scotland, Bodnant Garden in Wales, and Mount Stewart in Northern Ireland.

q.t: Which is England's largest national park, and what is its biggest stretch of water?
q.e: The Lake District is England's largest national park. It covers 885 square miles. It is famous for its lakes and mountains. The biggest stretch of water is Windermere.
o: Loch Lomond and the Trossachs, and Windermere

q.t:
Is the statement below TRUE or FALSE?
Most shops in the UK are open seven days a week, although trading hours on Sundays and public holidays are generally reduced.
q.e: Most shops in the UK are open seven days a week, although trading hours on Sundays and public holidays are generally reduced. Many towns also have markets on one or more days a week.

q.t: At what time do pubs usually open, and what is different on Sundays?
q.e: Pubs are usually open during the day from 11.00 am, 12 noon on Sundays. Night clubs with dancing and music usually open and close later than pubs. The licensee decides the hours that the pub or night club is open.
o: From 11.00 am, but from 12 noon on Sundays
From 12 noon, but from 11.00 am on Sundays
From 11.00 am every day including Sundays

q.t: Who decides the hours that a pub or night club is open?
q.e: Pubs are usually open during the day from 11.00 am. Night clubs with dancing and music usually open and close later than pubs. The licensee decides the hours that the pub or night club is open.

q.t: At 16, under what conditions may a person drink wine or beer?
q.e: To buy alcohol in a pub or night club you must be 18 or over. When they are 16, people can drink wine or beer with a meal in a hotel or restaurant, including eating areas in pubs, as long as they are with someone over 18.
o: With a meal in a hotel or restaurant, with someone over 18
Anywhere, as long as they are with someone over 18
With a meal in a hotel or restaurant, on their own
In a night club, with someone over 18

q.t: At what age can a person buy alcohol in a pub or night club?
q.e: To buy alcohol in a pub or night club you must be 18 or over, but people under that age may be allowed in some pubs with an adult. When they are 16, people can drink wine or beer with a meal in a hotel or restaurant as long as they are with someone over 18.

q.t: At what age can a person go into a betting shop or gambling club?
q.e: In the UK, people often enjoy a gamble on sports or other events. There are also casinos in many places. You have to be 18 to go into betting shops or gambling clubs.

q.t: What is the maximum fine for watching TV without a television licence?
q.e: Everyone in the UK with a TV, computer or other medium which can be used for watching TV must have a television licence. You will receive a fine of up to £1,000 if you watch TV but do not have a TV licence.

q.t: Which TWO groups get help with the cost of a television licence?
q.e: People over 75 can apply for a free TV licence and blind people can get a 50% discount. The money from TV licences is used to pay for the British Broadcasting Corporation.
o: People over 75, who can apply for a free licence
Blind people, who can get a 50% discount

q.t: Which of these statements is correct?
q.e: The BBC is a British public service broadcaster providing television and radio programmes. The BBC is the largest broadcaster in the world. It is the only wholly state-funded media organisation that is independent of government. Other UK channels are primarily funded through advertisements and subscriptions.
o: The BBC is the only wholly state-funded media organisation that is independent of government
The BBC is funded primarily through advertisements and subscriptions

q.t: What must all dogs in public places wear?
q.e: It is against the law to treat a pet cruelly or to neglect it. All dogs in public places must wear a collar showing the name and address of the owner. The owner is responsible for keeping the dog under control and for cleaning up after the animal in a public place.
o: A collar showing the name and address of the owner
A licence disc issued by the council
A collar showing the name of a veterinary surgeon

q.t:
Is the statement below TRUE or FALSE?
The official name of the country is the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland.
q.e: The official name of the country is the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland. 'Great Britain' refers only to England, Scotland and Wales, not to Northern Ireland.
